title: Peripheral whole blood DNA from fILD patient 1
extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.

extract_protocol_ch1: Genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral whole blood samples taken from patients enrolled in the UPitt cohort using the Puregene DNA isolation kit or QiaAmp blood DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) and from the UBC cohort using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen), all according to the manufacturer’s instructions. UBC samples were transferred to UPitt for simultaneous analysis alongside the UPitt samples. Prior to analysis, all DNA samples were stored at -20°C. DNA concentration and purity were assessed using the Infinite M200 Pro NanoQuant Plate Reader. Samples with an A260/A280 absorbance ratio outside of the 1.7-2.0 range were excluded.
hyb_protocol: Bisulphite converted DNA was amplified, fragmented, and hybridized to human Infinium MethylatioEPIC BeadChip (Illumina) using standard Illumina protocol.
scan_protocol: Arrays were imaged using BeadArray Reader (HiScan) and standard recommended Illumina scanner settings
data_processing: A multi-package approach to processing and analyzing raw DNAm data produced from the Infinium MethylationEPIC array was implemented. First, raw .idat files for each sample underwent pre-processing, quality control, filtering, and analysis using R statistical computing environment (version 4.2.1, www.r-project.org). Using the minfi package, samples with a mean detection p-value >0.05 were excluded (n=2). The detection p-value compares the total unmethylated and methylated signal at each CpG location and compares it to the background signal inferred from negative control probes, such that p-values >0.05 or >0.01 indicate a failed probe where the signal from the probe is not significantly different from the background. All samples are from blood, and thus it was not expected there would be major global differences in methylation patterns between the samples. This enabled normalization using a subset quantile procedure, which helps to mitigate the impacts of artifacts in the data that are the result of differences between Type-I and Type-II methylation probes and other technical sources of variation. Next, for probe filtering, we removed any CpG probes whose detection p-value was >0.01 on one or more samples. We also removed sex chromosome probes given that our study includes patients of male and female sex. Next, we removed probes that had a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at the CpG site, as this can result in impaired hybridization and detection of methylation for individuals with a variant allele at that locus. Subsequently, we removed cross-reactive probes that do not uniquely hybridize to a single CpG site on the MethylationEPIC array.
